The Canonical Workload box's Hardware row lists '80 GB each [1P][FACT]; 640 GB pool = [1P][FACT]' — the pool is arithmetic on the per-GPU constant, not a separately stated vendor fact. Table 4-2's deployment-unit row correctly gives the 640 GB pool as [1P][DERIVED], so the Canonical Workload box contradicts the ledger.
findings.fix_instruction: In the Canonical Workload box, change the Hardware row so the 640 GB pool carries [1P][DERIVED] (not [1P][FACT]), matching Table 4-2's composite-cell rule.

findings.evidence: "giving ~2.76M input and ~90K output tokens per $1 of fleet spend"
findings.issue: The stated derivation method (fleet spend per second) gives 3,000 ÷ 0.0333 ≈ 90,070 output tokens per $1, not exactly 90,000. The ~2.76M input figure (92,000 ÷ 0.0333 ≈ 2,762,762) correctly rounds to 2.76M, but the output figure is truncated rather than consistently rounded from the stated method. Minor rounding inconsistency between the two halves of the same sentence.
findings.fix_instruction: Either write ~90K as ~90.1K or explicitly note the rounding convention for both figures in the same cell (e.g. '~2.76M input and ~90K output, each rounded down from the stated division').

findings.page: PDF p.20 (printed xvi), PDF p.100 (printed 76), PDF p.104 (printed 80)
findings.chapter: Preface (Evidence boundary) / Ch. 4 (Table 4-2 and its Note 1)
findings.evidence: Preface, PDF p.20: "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known."  Ch. 4 Note 1, PDF p.104: "Axis 3 measurement status — how far it has climbed the measurement hierarchy: ANALYTICAL / SCENARIO-DERIVED / MODELED / MEASURED, or UNMEASURED." and "SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 stage a canonical-scenario value normally reports."  Table 4-2 row, PDF p.100: "Execution occupancy | ~86 / ~344 requests (at Wexec ≈ 8.6 s ...) | [canonical scenario][DERIVED] Little's Law L = λ × Wexec" — two tags only, no Axis-3 tag.
findings.issue: The book declares its own Axis-3 rule twice — the Preface requires Axis 3 to ride along with the label pair, and Ch. 4's Note 1 states that SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 status a canonical-scenario value 'normally reports' — but canonical-scenario values are then labelled with two tags only. Every row of the canonical-scenario provenance ledger (Table 4-2) and the derived canonical values carried through Ch. 1, Ch. 4, Ch. 6, Ch. 7 and Ch. 17 omit Axis 3, even though the book elsewhere uses standalone Axis-3 tags in prose ('That figure is an ANALYTICAL floor screen, not a measurement', PDF p.158; 'SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 stage a canonical-scenario value normally reports'). As written, a canonical-scenario value is formally unlabelled on Axis 3, so a reader cannot distinguish a canonical-scenario-derived figure from an ANALYTICAL bound from the label pair alone.
findings.fix_instruction: Either apply the declared rule — add the third tag to canonical-scenario rows and derived values (e.g. '[canonical scenario][DERIVED][SCENARIO-DERIVED]' in Table 4-2 and the values derived from it) — or, if Axis 3 is deliberately optional for canonical-scenario values, amend the Preface and Note 1 to say so explicitly (e.g. 'Axis 3 is implied by the provenance tag for [canonical scenario] values and stated explicitly only for ANALYTICAL/MEASURED claims'). Whichever way, make the two statements consistent so a reader can apply one rule.

findings.page: PDF p.98 (printed 74), PDF p.112 (printed 88), PDF p.115 (printed 91)
findings.chapter: Ch. 4 (§4.3 economic sidebar and Economic Constraints)
findings.evidence: Sidebar cell, PDF p.98: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K capex ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16) — owned, not rented, so ~half the cloud 21-host line."  §4.3, PDF p.112: "So the owned per-request cost is computed whole-fleet as (N_hosts × $20/hr) ÷ (rps × 3600) ≈ (6 × $20) ÷ (10 × 3600) ≈ ~$0.0033 per request at average" — where $20/hr is the cloud on-demand rental price.  Reconciliation note, PDF p.115: "the self-host 21-host line is a separate $155,816.93/month and is a distinct owned capex+energy cost basis, not a point in this cloud-rental series".
findings.issue: The word 'owned' carries two different meanings inside Ch. 4. In the $0.0033/$0.0140/$0.0029/$0.0056 per-request figures, 'owned fleet' means the fleet you operate yourself — and is explicitly computed from the cloud on-demand rental price of ~$20/hr, i.e. a rented fleet. In the sidebar and reconciliation note, 'owned' is used for the self-hosted capex+energy+staff total, and is contrasted with the cloud line as 'owned, not rented'. The same adjective therefore marks both the cloud-rental basis and its opposite within one chapter, while the chapter repeatedly warns that these figures are 'never cross-compared'. A reader quoting 'owned-fleet basis' cannot tell which of the two cost lines is meant.
findings.fix_instruction: Reserve 'owned' for the self-hosted capex+energy+staff line and rename the other basis consistently — e.g. 'self-operated fleet basis (rented GPU instances)' for the $0.0033/$0.0140/$0.0029/$0.0056 family, and 'self-host basis' for the $155,816.93 line. Update the six-figure reconciliation table's Basis column labels and the sidebar's 'owned, not rented' wording so the two terms cannot be read as the same thing.
